correctness.rationale: PASS. For each prime p and n>=0, Lucas digit factorization yields output digit d_i(x)=prod_j binom(x_j,i_j) mod p; the digit at output index p^j equals input digit x_j. For two different inputs with first mismatch j, all earlier output digits i<p^j agree and digit i=p^j differs; therefore the exact difference valuation is p^j, including j=0 and noninteger p-adic arguments by continuity. This gives injectivity, inverse digit recovery, compact closed image, and exactly p^J(N) output residues mod p^N with J(N)=min{j:p^j>=N} (N=1 gives 1). Each residue has Haar pushforward probability p^-J; covering by at most pN radius-p^-N balls gives Hausdorff and box dimension zero; image is uncountable, perfect, nowhere dense and Haar-null. Independently reconstructed 780 input-pair mismatches for each p=2,3,5; finite cases do not prove the all-p statement.

Mathonet–Rigo–Stipulanti–Zénaïdi 2022 define exactly t_p(n) and prove/illustrate Lucas-digit product relations; those facts are known. Their accessible full preprint concentrates on digit recurrences, regular sequences, Fermat/Roberts numbers and Gray/Nim patterns; it does not state the exact p-adic input/output valuation, topological closure, residue spectra, Haar law and zero-dimensionality. The present theorem logically derives stronger topological invariants. Possible implicit p-adic descriptions in older Pascal-attractor work remain an access risk.
